title: Ketamine’s Role in Alleged Cornell Rape Highlights Flood of Psychoactive Drugs on Campus - Nautilus
author: Christopher P. Holstege
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementHealthKetamine’s Role in Alleged Cornell Rape Highlights Flood of Psychoactive Drugs on CampusKetamine and many other psychoactive substances can’t be detected by most standard drug screens, so it’s unclear how often they play a role in sexual assault.CHBy Christopher P. Holstege7:00 AM CDT on October 30, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleFormer Cornell student Jane Doe, who filed a civil lawsuit in September 2026 alleging that seven fraternity members raped her at a party, said the young men who assaulted her pressured her into taking the drug ketamine.As an emergency room physician, medical toxicologist and the head of student health services at the University of Virginia, I have had a front-row seat to the growing danger that psychoactive substances such as ketamine present to the health and safety of university students.Ketamine and its emerging spin-off versions are part of a wave of new and evolving designer drugs entering the United States and other countries. How widely these substances are used remains unknown, since most hospitals are unable to detect them on standard urine drug screens. But ketamine and other drugs are being increasingly reported as agents used in sexual assault – either when people take these drugs voluntarily, are pressured to take them or are given them covertly.Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
